title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.

providers.name: Slack
providers.scope_notes: SAML SSO is available on Business+ and Enterprise, and on Free/Pro only with a connected Salesforce org. EMA uses organization-level installations and MCP user tokens.

controls.name: Require approved apps (Only allow pre-approved apps)
controls.what: Members can only install pre-approved apps; others must be requested and approved, and approval covers the scopes the app will use.
controls.setting: Admin > Apps and workflows > App Management Settings > Require approved apps
controls.quote: Apps connect third-party services to Slack, and by default, members can install them without approval from a Workspace Owner. If they'd like, Workspace Owners can enable app approval to pre-approve or restrict certain apps for their workspace.

controls.name: Restrict app
controls.what: Blocks members from installing or requesting a specific app; existing installs keep working until uninstalled.
controls.setting: Admin > Apps and workflows > Browse > [app] > Restrict
controls.quote: If an app you restrict has already been installed to your workspace, members can continue using it. You can uninstall any app you don't want people to use.

controls.name: App Management policy (Require App Approval)
controls.what: Turns on app approval for every workspace in the Enterprise org.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Settings > Organization Policies > Apps > App Management > Add Policy
controls.quote: Setting an app management policy turns on app approval for every workspace in an org. When app approval is enabled, members can only use apps that have been approved for their workspaces.

controls.name: Restrict for Organization
controls.what: Org Owners/Admins can block an app from being installed anywhere in the org when reviewing a request.
controls.setting: Org app request notification > Restrict for Organization; or admin.apps.restrict API
controls.quote: Select Approve for Organization or Restrict for Organization . Choosing Restrict for Organization will prevent all members from installing the app.

controls.name: Member Permissions: who can use the app
controls.what: Limits which members (everyone, no one, or specific people/groups) can initiate interaction with an installed app.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Integrations > Installed apps > [app] > Member Permissions > Who has permission to initiate interaction with this app
controls.quote: Choose who can use the app — Everyone , No one , or Specific people and groups .

controls.name: Remove or uninstall an org-level app
controls.what: Org admins can remove an org-installed app from workspaces or uninstall it from the whole org.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Integrations > Installed apps; or admin.apps.uninstall API
controls.quote: There are two options for removing apps installed at the org level: Remove the app from workspaces that no longer need to use it. Uninstall the app from your org to remove it from all workspaces.

controls.name: Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA)
controls.what: Lets the IdP (Okta) provision and govern access to the Slack MCP server from Claude via ID-JAG; Org Owner enables it and sets the issuer URL.
controls.setting: Organization settings > Security > SSO settings > Enterprise-Managed Authorization > Edit
controls.quote: Next to Enterprise-Managed Authorization, click Edit . Click the toggle to enable Enterprise-Managed Authorization. Review your ID-JAG issuer URL (ex. https://acmeinc.okta.com ) and verify that it’s correct.

controls.name: MCP client app approval
controls.what: MCP clients must be backed by a registered Slack app, so the normal app approval process gates MCP access.
controls.quote: MCP clients must be backed by a registered Slack app with a fixed app ID and hardcode that app ID. This allows Slack to: Let admins manage and approve your app/MCP client app using standard Slack app approval process.

controls.name: Restrict API Token Usage (Allowed IP Address Ranges)
controls.what: Rejects Web API, SCIM API and MCP server calls made with the app's tokens from IPs not on the list (max 20 IPv4 entries).
controls.setting: App settings > OAuth & Permissions > Restrict API Token Usage

no_control.what: Unlisted (non-Marketplace, non-internal) apps cannot use the Slack MCP server at all; admins cannot allow them.
no_control.quote: Only apps published in the Slack Marketplace and internal apps can use MCP at this time; unlisted apps are prohibited from using MCP.

controls_unknown: No tenant-admin IP allowlist for app tokens found; 'Restrict API Token Usage' IP ranges are set by the app developer in app config, not by workspace admins.
Whether admins can force-revoke individual user tokens without uninstalling the app.
Whether EMA lets admins restrict MCP scopes beyond IdP assignment.

authentication.summary: OAuth bot/user bearer tokens; app-level tokens for selected functions.

federation.details: Enterprise-managed authorization exchanges external IdP ID-JAGs for user access to Slack MCP. It is not general bot/workload federation.

ip_restriction.boundary: The app's Allowed IP Address Ranges (Restrict API Token Usage) also apply to Slack MCP server requests. The app owner sets the list, not the customer org admin; IPv6 is not supported.

renewal.summary: Obtain another MCP user token through the IdP/ID-JAG exchange.

administration.summary: Bot/user scopes, app approval/install controls, token revocation and rotation; EMA permissions delegated through IdP configuration.
administration.conditions: SAML SSO requires eligible Business+/Enterprise tiers. EMA uses organization-level installations and MCP user tokens.

sso.details: Tokens are issued only from an IdP credential, and IdP admins decide which permissions each user gets for the MCP server.

offboard.details: EMA returns xoxp user tokens, and Slack revokes a member's API tokens when the member is deactivated.

inventory.details: EMA apps are org-level installs, visible in Integrations > Installed apps; individual MCP tokens are not listed.

sso.ui: In the IdP: set which permissions each user gets for the Slack MCP server (token-exchange policy for audience https://mcp.slack.com/)

reads.ui: Organization settings > Security > Audit logs > Filter > Events

kill.ui: Remove the user's access to the app in the IdP; in Slack: Manage apps > Installed Apps > App Details > Configuration > Remove App

offboard.ui: Organization settings > People > Members > select > Deactivate

token_format.notes: EMA returns a user token (sample xoxp-) from POST /api/oauth.v2.user.access with grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer and an IdP-issued ID-JAG (expires_in 300). Access token expires_in 3600. MCP audience https://mcp.slack.com/.

log_sources.name: Slack Audit Logs API (GET https://api.slack.com/audit/v1/logs)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise plan. MCP tool calls logged as mcp_slack_*_tool_called; slack_ai_api_tool_called for API calls by AI apps.

log_sources.name: Identity provider system log (Okta)
log_sources.notes: ID-JAG issuance happens at the IdP; Okta is the only supported IdP for Slack MCP EMA in Claude. Event names not covered by Slack docs.

containment.steps: Remove the user's or app's access in the IdP (Okta) so no new ID-JAG is issued; uninstall or restrict the MCP client app in Slack; auth.revoke any captured xoxp token.
containment.notes: auth.revoke kills one access token at once, but the client's long-lived IdP credential can mint new tokens until the IdP or app side is revoked. EMA docs do not describe revocation.
